title: The Catch-All Rule
summary: Calls without a rule of their own go to a catch-all that wants the co-signer. Calls with their own rule never reach it.
lesson: The catch-all decides only for calls that have no rule of their own. Here it asks for the co-signer, so anything new needs a second opinion, while known payments flow without one. A call with its own rule is decided by that rule alone.

rules.note: Anything without its own rule needs the co-signer

steps.label: Pay Dave 500 USDC
steps.note: USDC transfers have their own rule, and Dave is on its list. The co-signer is not asked.

steps.label: Send 1 ETH to Erin
steps.note: No rule names this call, so the catch-all decides, and there is no co-signature.

steps.label: Pay Erin 500 USDC, co-signed
steps.note: USDC transfers have their own rule, so the catch-all is never asked. The co-signature cannot help: one rule decides each call, and Erin is not on its list.

steps.label: Delegatecall an unknown contract, co-signed
steps.note: This catch-all covers CALL only. DELEGATECALL has a catch-all of its own, and it is empty.
